newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Sri Lanka tenders to buy April 21-22 diesel, jet.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka tenders to buy April 21-22 diesel, jet.

text.p: Sri Lanka's state-owned Ceylon Petroleum Corp (CPC) has issued a tender to buy diesel and jet fuel for April 21-22 delivery, cost-and-freight (c-and-f) Colombo, a CPC source said on Wednesday.
The tender seeks 200,000 barrels of 1.0-percent sulphur diesel and 80,000 barrels of jet fuel.
The tender closes at 1500 hours Sri Lanka time on April 1 and offers will be valid for two days.
This tender came just a week after Sri Lanka awarded its last tender to buy 180,000 barrels of diesel and 80,000 barrels of jet fuel from Swiss trader Glencore for April 11-12 delivery.
The diesel portion was awarded at 47 cents per barrel above Singapore spot quotes and jet fuel at a 40-cent premium, c-and-f Colombo.

The source said the immediacy of the new tender came amid the ongoing drought in the country now into its sixth week, which has forced down water levels at the reservoirs and disrupting hydropower supplies.
The source said CPC might issue another tender to buy diesel and jet fuel for end April or early May delivery.
He said state utility Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB) will need to consume more diesel to drive generators to avoid power cuts which happened last year.

A senior CPC official said last month that Sri Lanka planned to import 700,000 tonnes of diesel this year. It bought 600,000 tonnes of diesel last year, up from the planned 300,000 tonnes because of drought.
